chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to visit the House (Kaaba) until morning [of Eid]. He said: Perhaps he delayed it until the days of Tashreeq pass, but he should not approach women or use perfume. The correct interpretation of these narrations is to apply them to one who is not a Mutamatti' (pilgrim performing Tamattu' Hajj), for he is given leeway to delay that [visiting the Kaaba] after the Day of Nahr (10th Dhu al-Hijjah) and the next day.

key_terms.التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) following Eid al-Adha
key_terms.النِّسَاءَ: Women (in the context of marital relations)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Nahr (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to perform Tawaf al-Ziyarah until the morning of Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration to resolve apparent contradictions in juristic opinions by distinguishing the Mutamatti' from other pilgrim types, granting them a specific window to delay Tawaf al-Ziyarah until after the Days of Tashreeq. The text highlights that while the act is deferred, the pilgrim remains in a state of Ihram, thereby maintaining prohibitions on marital relations and perfume until the ritual is completed. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the timing of the Kaaba's visitation for those performing Hajj al-Tamattu'.
